subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` remain a supported hard-enforcement surface for Telegram DMs, and if so should it be enforced through a shared direct-aware tool-policy resolver?
rationale: The schema and types already advertise a security-sensitive tool-policy surface, but current runtime enforcement does not read that direct config; choosing enforcement, retirement, or deferral changes operator security expectations and config compatibility.

options.title: Enforce Direct DM Tool Policy
options.body: Treat the existing direct `tools` and `toolsBySender` fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with exact, wildcard, account-scoped, threaded-DM, and sender-precedence tests.

options.title: Retire The Accepted Surface
options.body: If maintainers do not want DM-level hard enforcement, remove or reject the direct tool-policy config through doctor/docs so operators do not rely on a silent no-op.

options.title: Defer To Binding Policy Design
options.body: Keep this issue open but make the broader per-binding policy design the canonical product decision, accepting that Telegram direct policy remains unreliable until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct DM Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Treat the existing direct `tools` and `toolsBySender` fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with exact, wildcard, account-scoped, threaded-DM, and sender-precedence tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main history carries the central config and policy files under this contributor, and the decision spans config compatibility plus runtime security posture.
